findings.title: Sender validation is bypassed when no Integration row exists yet
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the Integration.DoesNotExist branch immediately returns pipeline.next_step() without comparing the pipeline's github_authenticated_user to the user who installed the GitHub app. Creation of the Integration row by the GitHub webhook is asynchronous and can race or be missed, so an attacker who knows or guesses a victim's incremental GitHub installation_id and starts the linking flow before that row exists can finish the pipeline; build_integration then creates/links the integration based only on installation_id. This defeats the new mismatch protection and can attach a victim's GitHub installation to the attacker's Sentry organization.

findings.title: Sender check crashes when Integration metadata has no sender
findings.body: The check dereferences integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] unconditionally. Integrations created through the pipeline itself only receive metadata.sender when state contains sender (build_integration), and no pipeline view binds sender into state, so pipeline-created or older orphaned ACTIVE integrations can lack metadata.sender. When such an integration exists without an OrganizationIntegration, dispatch raises KeyError/TypeError and returns a 500 instead of a graceful installation error or a successful relink.

findings.title: GitHub token exchange failures can raise instead of showing the installation error
findings.body: OAuthLoginView calls safe_urlopen for the OAuth access-token exchange outside the try block that only covers safe_urlread/parse_qsl, and then calls get_user_info without exception handling. If GitHub's token or user endpoints return an HTTP error, time out, or otherwise fail at the safe_urlopen layer, the exception propagates as an unhandled 500 rather than rendering the github-integration-failed page that the PR intends for bad or reused authorization codes. Both external calls need to be covered and mapped to the error response.

findings.title: Integration lookups do not filter by provider
findings.body: The lookups in GitHubInstallation use Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) even though Integration identity is unique only by (provider, external_id), not by external_id alone. If another integration provider has a record with the same external_id as a GitHub installation_id, get() raises MultipleObjectsReturned, which is not caught because only DoesNotExist is handled, causing a 500; it could also select the wrong integration's metadata for the sender comparison. The queries should filter provider to the GitHub provider key.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-not-found path
findings.body: The test stubs GET /app/installations/{id} to return 404, but its callback request supplies state ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which does not match the pipeline signature. OAuthLoginView therefore returns the generic invalid-installation page before GitHubInstallation/build_integration can call get_installation_info, so the test would pass even if the 404 handling in build_integration were broken or removed. The callback should use the valid pipeline state and assert the installation-not-found outcome.
